stem_en: Engineers editing files under packages/api never see the conventions written in packages/web/CLAUDE.md, and one of them files a bug about it. What is the correct assessment?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It is a bug: every CLAUDE.md in the repository, at any depth, is meant to load at session start, so discovery is broken here.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It is expected: a CLAUDE.md in a subdirectory loads on demand when Claude works in that subtree, so repository-wide conventions belong in the root CLAUDE.md.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The file is in the wrong place, because memory is discovered only at .claude/CLAUDE.md, so moving it there (rather than the package root) makes it load.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Memory files never cross package boundaries, so packages/web/CLAUDE.md has to be @imported from each other package's CLAUDE.md to reach those sessions.

explanation_ja: サブディレクトリの CLAUDE.md はそのサブツリーのファイルを扱うときにオンデマンドでロードされる。リポジトリ全体に適用したい規約はルートの CLAUDE.md(または .claude/rules/)に置く。よって B。A は階層の意図を誤解している。C は配置場所の問題ではない。D は他パッケージに無関係な規約まで取り込む設計になる。

stem_en: A 900-line CLAUDE.md mixes frontend, backend, and infrastructure rules. Engineers say Claude increasingly ignores parts of it, and every session loads all of it. Which reorganization is recommended?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Trim it to the 100 lines the team cites most often and delete the rest, so every session loads a short file that Claude can follow in full.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Move the file to the user level (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), where memory is read once per machine, so each session starts with a lighter footprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Split it into topic files under .claude/rules/, path-scoped where a topic applies to certain files only, leaving CLAUDE.md as a concise core.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Duplicate the file into each area's subdirectory, so frontend, backend, and infrastructure sessions each pick up their own copy on demand.

explanation_ja: 肥大化した CLAUDE.md は .claude/rules/ のトピック別ファイルに分割し、必要なものは paths で該当ファイル編集時だけロードするのが推奨構成である。よって C。A は必要な規約を失う。B はユーザーレベルに移すと共有されず、読み込み量も変わらない。D は重複管理を生み、同じ内容が何度もロードされる。

stem_en: Two engineers share the same repository. One, who edits Terraform files, sees the infrastructure conventions applied; the other, who only edits documentation, never does and suspects a broken setup. The conventions live in .claude/rules/infra.md with a paths frontmatter. What is the right diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Expected: a path-scoped rule loads only when a matching file is touched, and /context lists it under Memory files in the first engineer's session.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: A bug: rules committed to the repository are shared configuration, so both sessions should list the same Memory files whatever paths are edited.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: A precedence problem: the second engineer's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is read last and overrides the project rule, so clearing that user memory fixes it.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A placement problem: only the root CLAUDE.md reaches every session, so the conventions must be moved there (dropping the paths frontmatter).

explanation_ja: paths 付きの rule は該当ファイルを編集するセッションだけでロードされるので、ドキュメントしか触らないエンジニアに現れないのは仕様どおりである。/context の Memory files で実際のロード状況を確認できる。よって A。B は path-scoped rules の目的(無関係な文脈の削減)を否定している。C のユーザーレベル設定が project の rule を打ち消す仕組みは無い。D はロードを常時にしてしまい、削減の意図を失う。

stem_en: An engineer's /my-standup command pulls items from their personal calendar and applies their own Jira filter. They ask whether it should live in the repository's .claude/commands/ so that it "stays with the project". Which placement is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Project scope (.claude/commands/), so the command ships with the repository and teammates can review changes to it in pull requests.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Project scope, with the personal calendar and Jira filters stripped out before the command is committed to the repository.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: CLAUDE.md, since the routine runs every day and always-loaded memory keeps the steps available without invoking anything.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: User scope (~/.claude/commands/), because the command depends on personal data and would not make sense for teammates.

explanation_ja: 個人の予定や個人用フィルタに依存するコマンドはユーザースコープに置く。プロジェクトスコープはチームで共有する意味があるものの置き場所である。よって D。A と B は他人には無意味なコマンドをリポジトリに入れる。C は常時ロードの指示であり、起動して使う手順には向かない。

stem_en: A project skill /audit-deps runs the package manager and dumps thousands of lines of output into the main conversation, leaving little context for the actual work. Which SKILL.md frontmatter change isolates that output?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: allowed-tools: Bash, which pre-approves the package-manager commands so the audit runs without prompting for permission.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: context: fork, which runs the skill in an isolated context so that only its result returns to the main conversation.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: argument-hint, which asks for a package name up front so the audit is scoped to a single dependency, keeping the run short.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: disallowed-tools: Read, which stops the skill from reading large files, so bulky file contents stay out of the transcript.

explanation_ja: context: fork はスキルを隔離された文脈で実行し、冗長な出力や探索的な文脈がメイン会話を汚染しないようにする。よって B。A の allowed-tools は当該起動でのツールの事前許可であり、出力の隔離とは無関係。C の argument-hint は引数の入力を促す設定である。D は読み取りを禁じるだけで、コマンド出力の流入は止まらない。

stem_en: A team wants Claude Code to apply its logging conventions in every session, without anyone remembering to invoke anything. An engineer proposes packaging the conventions as a skill. What is the right placement?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A project skill committed to the repository, because skills are the recommended home for all shared conventions, logging included.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: A user-level skill installed on each engineer's machine, so the logging conventions follow them into every repository they work in.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: CLAUDE.md (or a path-scoped rule), because conventions that must always apply belong in memory that loads automatically, unlike skills.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A slash command (for example /logging-rules) that engineers run at the start of each session to pull the conventions into context.

explanation_ja: 常時適用したい規約は自動でロードされる CLAUDE.md や path-scoped rule に置く。スキルはオンデマンド起動なので、誰かが呼ばない限り効かない。よって C。A はスキルの用途(手順・稀に使う長い指示)を取り違えている。B はチーム共有にならず、しかも起動が必要。D も毎回の手動起動に依存する。

stem_en: A rule file .claude/rules/docs-style.md has the frontmatter paths: ["docs/**/*.md"]. It loads when editing docs/guide.md but not when editing the repository's top-level README.md, which should follow the same style. What is the cause and the fix?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The glob matches files under docs/ only; add README.md to paths, or widen the pattern to **/*.md so the root file matches too.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Rules do not apply to Markdown at all; the style guidance has to move into CLAUDE.md, which loads for every file a session touches.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Matching is by file name, so the rule file itself must be renamed README.md (in place of docs-style.md) before it takes effect.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Path-specific rules take effect only inside plan mode; planning the edit first would load the style rule for README.md as well.

explanation_ja: paths の glob に一致するファイルを編集するときだけ rule がロードされる。docs/**/*.md はルート直下の README.md に一致しないので、対象を paths に追加するか広いパターンにする。よって A。B は誤りで、rules はファイル種別を問わない。C はファイル名と一致条件は無関係。D は plan mode と rules は無関係である。

stem_en: Everything under services/billing/ — TypeScript, SQL migrations, YAML configs — must follow the billing team's conventions, and nothing outside that directory should. Which mechanism fits best?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A directory-level CLAUDE.md in services/billing/, since the conventions cover one subtree as a whole, whatever file type is edited.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Three glob-scoped rule files, one per file type, so TypeScript, SQL, and YAML each load only the conventions written for them.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The root CLAUDE.md, with the section marked "applies to services/billing only" so Claude can tell when the conventions are in scope.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A project skill that the billing team invokes before editing, which keeps the conventions out of context for the rest of the monorepo.

explanation_ja: 1 つのサブツリー全体に属する規約には、そのディレクトリの CLAUDE.md が最も適している。ファイル種別横断の規約に使う glob rule とは使い分ける。よって A。B は同じ規約を 3 つに分けて管理する無駄がある。C は常時ロードされ、注記だけでは適用範囲を機械的に限定できない。D は自動適用されない。

stem_en: An engineer is about to migrate the application's session storage from cookies to a token service. About 40 files are affected and two designs are both plausible. A colleague suggests "just start editing and see". Which approach is recommended?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Start editing directly: plan mode targets greenfield work, so on an existing codebase reading the files as you go is quicker.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Use plan mode first to survey the affected code and compare the two designs, then execute the plan once it has been approved.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Split the migration into 40 single-file tasks and run them one at a time, so each change stays small and reviewable on its own.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Ask Claude for the design document only, then implement the 40 files by hand so that every edit passes through human judgement.

explanation_ja: 多ファイルにまたがり、複数の妥当な設計があり、アーキテクチャ判断を含む変更は plan mode の典型的な対象である。計画を確認してから実行に移す。よって B。A は plan mode の適用条件を誤解している。C は設計判断を避けたまま作業を細切れにし、整合性が取れない。D は実装を Claude Code に任せる利点を捨てている。

stem_en: Before a refactor, the main Claude Code session must find every place where feature flags are evaluated across a large repository. The main context is already 60% used. How should the discovery be done?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Run Grep repeatedly in the main session until every call site is listed, so the refactor plan is built on results that stay in view.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Read every file that mentions the word "flag", so that no evaluation site is missed before the refactor plan is written.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Delegate the search to the Explore subagent, which returns a concise summary while keeping the verbose output in its own context.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Start a fresh main session with an empty context window, and redo the refactor planning there once the search has finished.

explanation_ja: 冗長な探索出力は Explore subagent に隔離させ、要約だけをメイン文脈に戻すのが Claude Code の推奨である。多段タスクでメイン文脈の枯渇を防げる。よって C。A と B は探索の出力がそのままメイン文脈を消費する。D は既に積み上げた計画の文脈を捨てることになる。

stem_en: An engineer describes an SQL-escaping helper in prose — "escape things the usual way, and handle the weird identifiers" — and each attempt from Claude Code differs. Which technique resolves this most directly?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Provide two or three concrete input/output examples, including an identifier containing quotes and a reserved word.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Ask Claude to produce five variations of the helper, then pick the one whose behaviour matches what you had in mind.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Lower the sampling temperature, so repeated runs converge on one implementation and the attempts stop diverging.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Expand the prose description with more precise adjectives covering the escaping rules and the unusual identifiers.

explanation_ja: 散文で一貫しない変換要件には、2〜3 個の具体的な入出力例が最も直接的である。引用符を含む識別子や予約語のようなエッジケースも例で示す。よって A。B は要件を確定せずに当てずっぽうを増やす。C は出力のばらつきを減らしても、要件そのものは曖昧なままである。D は曖昧さの原因である散文を増やしている。

stem_en: An engineer needs a webhook retry policy but is unsure about the requirements — backoff limits, idempotency, what to do after repeated failures. Which way of working with Claude Code surfaces those considerations before code is written?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Ask Claude to write the retry policy immediately, then iterate on the gaps as failures turn up during testing.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Write the specification alone first — backoff, idempotency, final failure — and involve Claude only afterwards.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Lower the sampling temperature, so that Claude makes fewer assumptions about the unstated parts of the policy.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Use the interview pattern: have Claude interview you about the requirements first, and implement afterwards.

explanation_ja: 未知の領域では、実装前に Claude に質問させる interview pattern が考慮事項(バックオフ上限・冪等性・最終失敗時の扱い)を引き出す。よって D。A は暗黙の前提のまま実装し、後から手戻りが増える。B は Claude の知識を活用せず時間もかかる。C は温度と要件の洗い出しは無関係である。

stem_en: A nightly job already runs claude -p with --output-format json, yet the downstream dashboard still breaks: the result field is a free-form summary whose structure changes from night to night. What should the job add?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: --verbose, so the job emits the full turn detail and the dashboard can read the fields it needs.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: --json-schema with the required shape, so the structured result always conforms to it.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: A regular expression layer that pulls the dashboard's fields out of the summary text.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A second prompt, run after the first, that asks the model to reformat its own answer.

explanation_ja: --output-format json は応答全体を JSON で包むが、モデルが返す結果そのものの形状までは固定しない。形状は --json-schema で指定する。よって B。A は詳細が増えても構造は保証されない。C は文言の揺れでパーサーが壊れる、まさに現在の問題である。D は自己整形で形状の保証は得られない。

stem_en: A CI pipeline lets Claude Code generate a fix, then starts a separate reviewer instance but feeds it the generator's full transcript "for context". The reviewer approves nearly everything. What should change?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Give the reviewer only the diff and explicit review criteria, so its judgement is not anchored to the generator's choices.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Run the review inside the generator's own session, which saves tokens and keeps every decision already in context.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Feed the reviewer the transcript twice, once as background and once as the review target, so it reads the reasoning closely.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Replace the reviewer instance with a linter, whose rules are deterministic and cannot be talked into approving a change.

explanation_ja: 独立インスタンスにレビューさせる目的は、生成側の推論文脈を持たない視点を得ることにある。生成側の履歴を渡すとその判断に引きずられ、独立性が失われる。よって A。B は自己レビューの限界そのものである。C は anchoring を強めるだけ。D は静的解析で捕まらない設計上の問題を見落とす。
